LinkedIn lead sourcing

Build clean LinkedIn lead lists from Sales Navigator, posts or your own files

Good outreach starts with the list. Connectora gives you three ways to build one, and checks every profile before a single invitation goes out.

Book a demoAll features
Sources

Where can Connectora get leads from?

Connectora builds lead lists from three sources: a LinkedIn Sales Navigator search, the people who reacted to or commented on a LinkedIn post, and your own CSV, TSV or Excel file of LinkedIn profile URLs. Every profile is validated and de-duplicated, and anyone already contacted by another campaign is skipped.

SourceBest forKey limit
Sales Navigator searchPrecise ICP targeting by title, company size, industry and regionUp to 2,500 people per search (LinkedIn's own cap); needs an active Sales Navigator seat
LinkedIn post engagersWarm prospects who already showed interest in a topicReads are paced daily to protect the account
File uploadLists from your CRM, events, data providers or past campaignsUp to 25 MB and 50,000 rows per file
Sales Navigator

How do I turn a Sales Navigator search into a lead list?

Run your search in LinkedIn Sales Navigator, copy the page URL, and paste it into Connectora's Lead Generation screen with a connected account that has a Sales Navigator seat. Choose how many people to pull, up to 2,500. Connectora pages through the results at an irregular pace, removes duplicates, and lets you export a CSV.

  1. Pick the account to search from. Only healthy, connected accounts are offered, and you see its name and headline to confirm.
  2. Build the search in Sales Navigator with your filters, then copy the browser URL.
  3. Paste the URL and choose a target: 250, 500, 1,000, 2,000 or the maximum of 2,500.
  4. Watch progress and stop at any time. Pages are requested at random intervals, never on a fixed beat.
  5. Review the results. Each person is tagged where relevant: Open (can be messaged without connecting), Premium, or Invited (an invitation is already pending).
  6. Export to CSV with seven columns: First Name, Last Name, Title, Company, Location, LinkedIn URL and Headline. Then upload it to a campaign; the URL column is detected automatically.

Connectora shows both how many people match your search and how many LinkedIn will actually return, so a 9,000-person search never looks like a failed export.

Post engagers

How do I get leads from a LinkedIn post's likes and comments?

Paste the URL of a LinkedIn post into Connectora. It identifies the post and its author, then collects the people who reacted to it and commented on it, removing anyone who did both so they appear once. You get a list with name, headline, company, connection degree and a validated profile URL, ready for a campaign.

Why it works: someone who reacted to a post about your topic has already signalled interest. A connection note that references the post is relevant by default.

Good posts to use:

  • Your own posts and your team's posts.
  • Posts by industry voices on a problem you solve.
  • Event or webinar announcement posts in your niche.

Post lookups count toward each account's daily activity, so Connectora paces them to leave room for your campaigns.

File upload

How do I upload my own lead list?

Drag a CSV, TSV, XLSX or XLS file into the campaign wizard. Connectora finds the header row and the LinkedIn URL column on its own, then checks every row. Valid profiles are standardised, rows without a first name are flagged, and invalid or duplicate rows are listed with a reason and never contacted.

The upload is step 2 of the campaign wizard.

Row statusExample reasonContacted?
ValidRewritten to https://www.linkedin.com/in/<name>Yes
WarningNo first name, so {firstName} would be blankYes
Invalid"This is a company page, not a personal profile" or "linkedn.com is not a valid domain, did you mean linkedin.com?"No
Duplicate"Duplicate of row 14 (same profile)"No
  • Every column becomes a variable. Upload a column called "Pain point" and use {Pain point} in your messages.
  • Common column names are recognised, such as first name, last name, company, title and email.
  • No LinkedIn URL column? Connectora stops and tells you which column to rename.
De-duplication

How does Connectora prevent contacting the same person twice?

Connectora keeps a record of every person your workspace has contacted. When a lead in a new campaign was already contacted by another campaign, it is skipped with the note "Already contacted in campaign …". Within a single file, repeat profiles are flagged as duplicates before launch.

This protects your reputation with prospects and your accounts' acceptance rate, which is one of the signals LinkedIn watches.

FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Only for Sales Navigator searches. File uploads and campaigns work with standard LinkedIn accounts.

No. Connectora is focused on LinkedIn outreach. If your file includes an email column, it is kept with the lead.

A single upload can contain up to 50,000 rows. Daily limits decide when each lead is contacted, never how many you can upload.

It depends on your jurisdiction and purpose. Process personal data only where you have a lawful basis (for example legitimate interest under GDPR), keep messages relevant, and honour opt-out requests.
